nodes.label: Scroll Cinema Homepage Hero — Implementation Plan
Act-timeline invariant: act boundaries in lib/cinema.ts ACTS and the scene's PHASES are the same numbers — single source of truth, no drift
nodes.rationale: Original six acts (boot 0-0.12, assembly, dive, bull, flash, handoff to 1.0); a comment in each file points at the other so choreography and math never diverge.

nodes.label: Offline frame pipeline (npm run cinema:capture): Playwright screenshots real pages → deterministic scene.html renderAt(t) steps 160 frames → ffmpeg WebP encode + manifest + poster
nodes.rationale: Hybrid $0-budget production: UI acts are code-rendered from real app screenshots (AI video garbles UI text); frames are committed to public/cinema/frames/ and served as static assets, budgets ≤9MB desktop / ≤3MB mobile.

nodes.label: Copy beats and the green flash as DOM overlays synced to scroll progress — crisp, accessible, SEO-visible, never baked into frames
nodes.rationale: Baking text into frames would blur it and hide it from search engines; DOM overlays driven by the same timeline config keep copy editable without re-rendering frames.

nodes.label: Placeholder-first bull: seeded green particle silhouette ships until the user generates the Veo bull.mp4; swap is a pipeline re-run, zero code changes
nodes.rationale: Veo free tier credits are limited so the prompt ships refined rather than iterated; the pipeline detects bull.mp4, extracts and color-grades frames with ffmpeg, and the scene cross-fades from particles to footage automatically.
